Show tunes, as a distinct genre of music, have their roots in the United States, particularly in the context of Broadway musicals. However, it is essential to recognize that this genre has been influenced by various musical traditions from around the world. 

The development of show tunes can be traced back to the late 19th and early 20th centuries when American composers and lyricists began incorporating elements from popular music styles, such as ragtime, jazz, and operetta, into their theatrical productions. These influences, combined with the unique storytelling approach of American musical theatre, gave birth to the show tunes genre.

Show tunes are characterized by their catchy melodies, strong lyrics, and diverse styles, ranging from ballads and uptempo numbers to comedic songs and dramatic pieces. They often feature full orchestration, further enhancing their emotional impact and storytelling capabilities. Over time, show tunes have continued to evolve, incorporating elements from various musical genres and cultures, making them a rich and dynamic art form.
